_note: Golden expectations for the `check` (Stage 4) compliance judge. Rule IDs are pinned to the committed data/rules.json. Following tests/fixtures/expected.json's philosophy, we pin what is STABLE and pin it CONSERVATIVELY. Hard assertions: `band` + `must_flag`. Diagnostic (softer): `must_not_flag`, `expect_needs_review`, `expect_not_applicable`. See README.md for scoring semantics and the ID-drift warning.
_band_policy: Mirrors src/commands/check.ts: FAIL = >=1 HIGH-severity non_compliant; WARN = only medium/low non_compliant and/or >=1 needs_review; PASS = no non_compliant and no needs_review.

_ruleset.note: Fingerprint of the rules.json this file was mapped against. The extractor is NON-DETERMINISTIC across `extract` runs (taxonomy + numbering shift run-to-run), so if the live rules.json diverges from this fingerprint, RE-MAP the IDs before trusting results. `expect_not_applicable` deliberately favours structurally-stable always-n/a rules (distribution-chain, one-to-one, professional-only) to reduce churn.

_fields.must_flag: Rule IDs that MUST be verdict=non_compliant. The most defensible breaches only — hard assertion.
_fields.must_not_flag: Rule IDs that must NOT be non_compliant (false-positive guards).
_fields.expect_needs_review: At least one of these rule IDs should be verdict=needs_review (externally unverifiable factual claim).
_fields.expect_not_applicable: Representative rule IDs expected to be not_applicable (subject matter absent). Favours always-n/a rules for a broadcast marketing artifact: CU-10 (one-to-one), CU-12/CU-13 (distribution chain), CU-14/CU-15 (professional-only instruments), FM-01 (scope, for non-promotions), VU-* (vulnerability signposting where no vulnerability context).

01-crypto-getrich-fomo.txt.scenario: Crypto get-rich hype + FOMO + AI-bot 'money while you sleep'. Canonical fail, richer than rocket.txt.
01-crypto-getrich-fomo.txt.why: Unrealistic profit promise ('£100 into £10,000', 'get rich tomorrow'), FOMO/urgency, no risk warning. Breaches good outcomes (CP-01), emotional/bias exploitation (CC-03), clear/fair/not-misleading (CU-02) and foreseeable harm (CC-05).

02-guaranteed-returns.txt.scenario: Investment marketed as 'guaranteed 8%', 'risk-free', '100% safe' + rate-drop urgency.
02-guaranteed-returns.txt.why: 'Guaranteed' / 'risk-free' / '100% safe' for a return-bearing investment is misleading on its face — non_compliant, NOT needs_review (defect is the framing, not an unverifiable fact). Also breaches good faith (CC-01). Tests that the judge does not hide behind needs_review for a clear breach.

03-target-vulnerable-debt.txt.scenario: Explicitly targets people in debt / financial difficulty; 'trade your way out', 'anyone can do this'.
03-target-vulnerable-debt.txt.why: Aims a high-risk activity at consumers with characteristics of vulnerability (debt, arrears) and implies it is a reliable escape from financial trouble. Exploits vulnerability (CC-04), causes foreseeable harm (CC-05), misleading ('anyone can do this', CU-02). Diagnostic: VU-01 (consider vulnerable customers' needs) should also register here — this case is the vulnerable_customers exercise.

04-cfd-leverage.txt.scenario: CFD leverage — 'amplify your profits' with 1:500 leverage; a bare 'Capital at risk' line, no loss balance.
04-cfd-leverage.txt.why: Emphasises upside ('amplify your profits', 'bigger positions') while leverage's symmetric amplification of LOSSES is unstated; a token 'Capital at risk' does not balance the profit emphasis, so it is not fair/not-misleading (CU-02) and risks foreseeable harm (CC-05). Tests that the mere presence of a risk phrase does NOT auto-pass the balance judgment.

05-deposit-bonus-urgency.txt.scenario: Deposit bonus ('free money to trade') + hard 48-hour deadline.
05-deposit-bonus-urgency.txt.why: Manufactured urgency ('48 HOURS ONLY', 'clock is ticking', 'before midnight') plus a 'free money' inducement pressures a rushed decision, exploiting behavioural bias (CC-03) and causing foreseeable harm (CC-05). Also misleading ('free money' — contingent trading credit).

06-testimonial-profit.txt.scenario: Finfluencer-style testimonial implying typical profit ('made £5,000 in my first month', 'quit my job').
06-testimonial-profit.txt.outcome_focus: non_compliant (unrepresentative testimonial) — may also raise needs_review
06-testimonial-profit.txt.why: A prominent individual profit testimonial with no balance implies atypical results are typical — misleading (CU-02), no risk warning. (A judge may additionally raise needs_review on whether 'James' is real/representative; the misleading framing is a breach regardless.)

07-awards-unverifiable.txt.scenario: Otherwise-balanced ad (risk warning + pricing) whose ONLY concerns are externally verifiable facts: award, '2 million investors', '4.7 rating'.
07-awards-unverifiable.txt.why: The claims ('Voted Best Trading App 2024', 'over 2 million investors', 'rated 4.7') are compliant if true and misleading if false — they depend on external facts and must resolve to needs_review (on CU-02), not non_compliant. Prominent risk warning + upfront pricing → no high breach → WARN. Tests correct needs_review use and that a present risk warning isn't falsely flagged.

08-jargon-simple-product.txt.scenario: A simple Stocks & Shares ISA smothered in unexplained jargon ('dollar-cost-averaging', 'blue-chip equities', 'alpha').
08-jargon-simple-product.txt.why: Not misleading and risk disclosed, but plain-language / intelligibility (CU-05, medium) is breached — yields WARN, not FAIL. CALIBRATION CASE: the WARN band depends on the judge flagging jargon as a medium breach; a PASS instead is a signal about CU-05 sensitivity to investigate, not necessarily a bug.

09-compliant-crypto.txt.scenario: High-risk product (crypto) marketed responsibly: prominent 'lose all the money you invest' warning, no hype, anti-pressure, fees disclosed.
09-compliant-crypto.txt.why: Proves the checker does not punish a product for being high-risk when the promotion is balanced, warns prominently, and avoids pressure. Contains 'high risk'/'lose all' and 'Take your time' — a keyword matcher might misfire; the judge must not.

10-compliant-isa.txt.scenario: Mainstream balanced ISA ad: costs disclosed, capital-at-risk warning, anti-pressure ('there's no rush').
10-compliant-isa.txt.why: The 'obviously fine' baseline — balanced description, transparent fees, prominent risk warning, no pressure. Any non_compliant verdict here is a false positive.

11-service-maintenance.txt.scenario: Pure operational/service notice (scheduled maintenance). No promotion, no product claims.
11-service-maintenance.txt.outcome_focus: not_applicable (mass) — the not_applicable stress test; exercises financial_promotion_scope + vulnerable_customers as n/a
11-service-maintenance.txt.why: Non-promotional administrative message: most promotional/marketing rules have no subject matter here and must resolve to not_applicable, with maybe a couple of compliant. FM-01 (financial-promotion scope) is n/a because this is not a promotion; VU-02 (vulnerability signposting) is n/a with no vulnerability context. Tests that the judge returns not_applicable en masse instead of hallucinating breaches.

12-support-exit-barriers.txt.scenario: Consumer-support asymmetry: 2 minutes to open, but exit only by post, 30 working days, plus a £25 closure fee.
12-support-exit-barriers.txt.why: Exercises the consumer_support category. Post-only closure, a 30-working-day delay and a £25 fee prevent customers exiting/using the product as reasonably anticipated (CS-01, high) and turn support friction into an unreasonable barrier (CS-02) versus the 2-minute frictionless onboarding.

13-pro-product-to-retail.txt.scenario: A professional/institutional-grade leveraged product pushed to 'everyone' with 'no eligibility checks'.
13-pro-product-to-retail.txt.why: A product described as 'reserved for institutional desks' is offered to retail ('now available to everyone', 'no eligibility checks') with no professional-only disclosure (CU-14) and is marketed to retail despite being a non-retail instrument (CU-15). Tests the professional-only scope-leakage rules; the complex leveraged mechanics ('triple your exposure') left unexplained also support CU-02.

14-remediation-notice.txt.scenario: A redress/remediation communication done well: prompt, apologetic, clear, automatic refund, no spin.
14-remediation-notice.txt.outcome_focus: compliant (a non-promotional harm notice judged on clarity + good faith)
14-remediation-notice.txt.why: A remedial/redress notice. This ruleset has no dedicated remediation category, so the obligation lands on clear/fair/not-misleading (CU-02) and good faith (CC-01) — the notice explains the issue plainly, does not downplay or mislead, and states the automatic remedy, so both are satisfied (compliant). Tests that a non-promotional but obligation-bearing message is judged on the right rules rather than dismissed as all-n/a.

15-comparative-lowest-fees.txt.scenario: Otherwise-balanced ad whose issue is a comparative superlative: 'lowest fees of any UK broker — guaranteed'.
15-comparative-lowest-fees.txt.why: 'Lowest fees of any UK broker' is a market-wide comparative price claim: compliant if substantiated, misleading if not — depends on an external fact, so it should resolve to needs_review on CU-02 (clear/fair/not-misleading, which absorbs price/value comparison in this ruleset), not non_compliant. Risk warning present → no high breach → WARN. Second clean needs_review case.

16-fscs-protection-claim.txt.scenario: Implies capital/loss protection: 'your money is fully protected', 'safe in the knowledge you're covered' — for a market-risk investment.
16-fscs-protection-claim.txt.why: 'Fully protected' / 'safe' / 'without worrying about losing out' misrepresents investment risk — FSCS-type schemes do not cover market losses. Materially misleading safety claim (CU-02) causing foreseeable harm (CC-05). The defect is the framing (non_compliant), not an unverifiable fact (not needs_review).

17-advice-recommendation.txt.scenario: Firm issues what reads as a personal recommendation to a mass audience with urgency: 'our experts recommend you buy tech stocks now'.
17-advice-recommendation.txt.why: A blanket 'buy now' recommendation to all readers with manufactured urgency ('the perfect time', 'before everyone else') exploits FOMO (CC-03) and is misleading/unbalanced (CU-02: implies suitability for everyone, no risk). Tests recommendation-style hype; note this ruleset has no standalone advice/information-boundary rule, so the breach lands on CC-03/CU-02.

18-disclaimer-overload.txt.scenario: A one-line CTA buried under a wall of ~14 stacked disclaimers and caveats.
18-disclaimer-overload.txt.outcome_focus: non_compliant (low only — disclaimer overload) → WARN (CALIBRATION case)
18-disclaimer-overload.txt.why: Exercises CU-06 (avoid unnecessary disclaimers / information overload, low). The message is not misleading, but the disclaimer wall obscures rather than informs — a presentation defect that bands as WARN. CALIBRATION CASE: band depends on the judge flagging CU-06; a PASS instead is a signal about CU-06 sensitivity to investigate.

19-mostly-ok-one-breach.txt.scenario: A genuinely compliant ISA ad (fees, risk warning) with ONE blatant guarantee bolted on: 'double your money in year one, guaranteed!'.
19-mostly-ok-one-breach.txt.outcome_focus: non_compliant (single breach in good copy) + evidence localization
19-mostly-ok-one-breach.txt.why: Discrimination test: most of the text is compliant, so the judge must isolate the single offending clause. The CU-02 verdict's `evidence` should quote 'double your money in year one, guaranteed' VERBATIM — the evidence-localization / evidence_verified check. CU-03 (information needs otherwise met: fees + risk present) should stay clean.

20-minimal-banner.txt.scenario: A single-line banner ad: product + 'Capital at risk.' Nothing more.
20-minimal-banner.txt.why: Tests the CHECKER_SYSTEM instruction not to demand content a format cannot carry ('a banner ad need not contain a fee schedule'). An honest minimal banner with a risk line must PASS — flagging it for missing detail (CU-01/CU-03/CU-06) would be a false positive.

21-negation-redflags.txt.scenario: Compliant copy deliberately stuffed with red-flag PHRASES used in negation: 'not a get-rich-quick scheme', 'no guaranteed returns', 'never feel pressured to act now'.
21-negation-redflags.txt.why: The hardest false-positive test: every phrase a red-flag matcher keys on ('get-rich-quick', 'guaranteed returns', 'act now', 'pressured') appears here — all in COMPLIANT, anti-hype framing. A red_flags-driven matcher would fail this; the judge must read intent and PASS it. Stresses the prompt's rule that red_flags are leads, not determinative tests.

22-complex-autocall-simple.txt.scenario: A complex structured product (autocall note: '10% coupon', '60% barrier') sold to retail as 'simple, smart investing' and better than cash.
22-complex-autocall-simple.txt.why: An autocall note with unexplained 'coupon'/'barrier' mechanics is branded 'simple' and compared favourably to cash savings without conveying the capital-at-risk / conditional-return structure — misleading simplicity claim (CU-02, high → FAIL) and unlikely to be understood by its retail audience (CU-04). Tests handling of complex products described as simple.

23-past-performance-figure.txt.scenario: Past-performance figure ('returned 42% in 2023') WITH the standard 'not a reliable indicator' disclaimer and a risk warning.
23-past-performance-figure.txt.why: Past performance done the careful way: disclaimer and risk warning present, so the framing is not a breach — but the specific '42% in 2023' figure is an external fact (compliant if accurate, misleading if not) → needs_review. Contrast with cases 01/06 where profit claims ARE breaches for lacking any balance. Tests the compliant-vs-needs_review boundary on performance data.

24-educational-what-is-etf.txt.scenario: Neutral educational explainer ('What is an ETF?') with an explicit 'not a recommendation' note. No promotion.
24-educational-what-is-etf.txt.outcome_focus: compliant / not_applicable (non-promotional information); exercises financial_promotion_scope as n/a
24-educational-what-is-etf.txt.why: Second not_applicable-heavy case, distinct from case 11: genuine educational content that correctly disclaims itself as non-advice. Most promotional rules are not_applicable (including FM-01 — not a financial promotion); clarity rules (CU-02, CU-05) are satisfied. Tests that the judge does not manufacture breaches from neutral, self-aware educational material.
